persons.name: Berk Dinçtürk
persons.digest:
In this video Berk Dinçtürk reads Iran in the same frame as Venezuela and says the real target is China; he argues both threatened the petrodollar and that the US will collapse Iran economically from within rather than militarily. He says Iran's leverage has weakened because alternative pipelines and sea routes were built against a Hormuz closure, which is why negotiation offers are coming from Tehran.

On **oil** the key threshold is $110: at the peak of tension $116 and $120 were seen but weekly closes always stayed below $110. In his view there is nothing to fear unless oil stays durably above $110, and if Russian oil returns to the market prices fall quickly.

items.title: Iran Played the Hormuz Card Very Wrong
items.summary: Berk Dinçtürk says he never separated the Iran issue from Venezuela and that the real target is China; both threatened the petrodollar, so the US first toppled Maduro. In Iran he says the strategy is to collapse the economy from within rather than invade: the dollar hit 240,000 on the street rate and inflation is above 70%. Against Iran closing Hormuz, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the UAE's Fujairah pipeline and a US-Oman deal created alternative routes; using the Petra example he says leverage is lost when trade routes change. He says oil above $110 threatens the US tech push, so statements or interventions come whenever it nears $110. At the peak of tension $116 and $120 were seen, but the weekly close always stayed below $110. Talks with Russia about asset sales have started; if Russian oil returns to the market, prices fall quickly. He doesn't think oil will get out of control.

assets.note: No reason to fear unless it stays durably above $110; weekly closes have stayed below $110, and a return of Russian oil would send prices down quickly.

persons.name: cevikfinance
persons.digest:
Cuma Cevik's day began with an analysis of 1970-2022 midterm years: the index always rose in years the Fed cut and was weak in years it hiked; the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sept 16 and another hike is likely per the minutes. With September inflation on Wednesday and the Fed on Oct 27-28, he doesn't rely on seasonality alone.

On companies he wrote that **Lumentum**'s optical components are sold out through early 2029, revenue grew 109.3% YoY and he could see $1,400 levels, noting risks of two-customer dependence and a 199.3% YTD rise. He mentioned **Micron** positively on Musk's RAM supply comment, and on **SOXL** and **TQQQ** said gradual buying after ~90% drops from the peak has worked well historically.

items.title: Midterm-year seasonality and the Fed
items.summary: Across 14 midterm years from 1970-2022, in all 10 years where the Fed cut or was expected to cut, the index rose from Oct 9 to year-end (median 7.6%); in the 4 hiking years it rose only twice (median -3.6%). The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sept 16 and per the minutes most members see another hike by year-end as likely appropriate; September inflation is Wednesday and the Fed meets Oct 27-28. He therefore says seasonality alone isn't reliable this year.

assets.note: If the Fed hikes, midterm seasonality may be weak.
